category_title: Preschoolers with aggressive behaviors and social-emotional regulation challenges
minimal_context: Joshua is participating in free play activities and is expected to share toy trucks with a classmate.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Joshua, it is time for free play. You and your classmate can play with the toy trucks together.

STUDENT: I am the boss of the trucks. You have to be the bad guy and I get the big truck.

TUTOR: Let's try to share the toys and play nicely.

STUDENT: (Growls at his classmate) No! We have to play my way!

TUTOR: Joshua, please use your words. What do you think is a good way to play together?

STUDENT: (Yells and throws a toy truck) Do this or I will hurt you!

options.A: Write classroom rules for appropriate play, cooperation, and following directions, supported with Boardmaker™ pictures, and verbally review them daily.
options.B: Place an exclusive display board in the classroom solely for Joshua to display his work during activities.
options.C: Put tremendous effort into improving Joshua's study techniques and increasing his ability to take initiative during activities.
options.D: Implement simultaneous stimulation of nonverbal communication from the perspective of total communication during daily free play activities.
